signal.title: wagmi v2 multi-chain wallet integration — production scale

signal.interpretation: This predicts genuine comfort with the wallet UX lifecycle — connect/disconnect, chain-switching, transaction broadcasting, error states. The v2-specific citation suggests the candidate tracked the API surface change, not just carried forward existing code.

signal.title: Turborepo monorepo — CI outcome ownership
signal.observation: Profile: Turborepo migration at DeFi Protocol reduced CI time by 60%. GitHub signals confirm turbo.json in recent repos (structural pattern, High-confidence). The 60% figure is a measurable outcome tied to a specific employer context — not a vague 'improved CI' claim.
signal.interpretation: Candidate has owned the monorepo infrastructure decision end-to-end, not just consumed it. The CI metric implies measurement discipline and awareness of cross-team impact — directly relevant for a team adopting Turborepo across product lines.

signal.title: Radix UI design system — cross-team adoption
signal.observation: Radix-based design system: headless primitives, Zod-validated component APIs, Storybook, Chromatic visual regression, adopted across 4 product teams. GitHub signals confirm @radix-ui and storybook as active dependencies. Both profile specificity and GitHub corroboration present.

signal.title: Zod schema validation — applied across architectural layers
signal.observation: Zod appears in: stack listing, design system (Zod-validated component APIs), and GitHub signals (active dependency in recent repos). Three independent evidence sources for the same technology.

signal.observation: DeFi Trading Dashboard cites WebSocket price feeds and sub-100ms render performance at 500k MAU. The performance threshold is stated as a concrete target, not a vague claim.

gaps.gap: Smart contract write-path depth not evidenced
gaps.mitigation: DeFi Trading Dashboard cites ERC-721/1155 transaction flows in the NFT Marketplace, which implies frontend-initiated contract writes. Depth of ABI integration (read vs. write, error decoding, gas estimation) is best probed in the interview — the adjacent evidence is strong enough that absence of a direct claim is not disqualifying.

interview_hooks: The DeFi Trading Dashboard specifically cites wagmi v2 — that was a significant API change from v1. Walk me through one concrete migration decision you made (a pattern that changed or a hook that disappeared) and how you handled the cross-team rollout at a 500k-MAU product.

Your Turborepo migration reduced CI time by 60% at DeFi Protocol. Eighteen months on, what is the actual ongoing maintenance overhead compared to the monolith — and if you were starting the same migration today with what you know now, what would you change about the approach?

The NFT Marketplace uses server-side blockchain data fetching in Next.js App Router rather than client-side RPC calls. That is a deliberate architectural choice. Walk me through why you landed there — what failure modes were you solving for, and what are the tradeoffs you accepted (e.g., caching latency, SSR cost on-chain vs. off-chain)?

Your Radix-based design system was adopted across 4 product teams. Adoption across teams usually requires more than technical quality — walk me through one case where another team pushed back on the system and how you resolved it without owning their codebase.
